raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's planning. I'm sitting here at the kitchen table with my wife, working through what needs to be done.

---

**My thinking this year:**

I'm 64. Been farming this land for 45 years — started back when it was still the production team. Me and the old lady are the only ones here now. The kids are in the city, they send money at New Year but they're not coming back to pick cotton.

Thirteen and a half mu. Not a lot, not tiny either. I do it the same way most years — about 8 mu of cotton on the west plot (sandier soil, cotton likes it), and the other 5.5 mu I do wheat-maize double crop. That gives us our flour for the year, the maize for selling or feeding chickens, and the cotton is the cash crop.

**On cotton** — honestly, it's getting harder every year. The picking wears us out. Some neighbors in the village have quit cotton and gone all-grain, but I know cotton. I know when to water, when to spray for bollworm, when to top the plants. The extension guy came around last fall talking about some new variety, but I'm going to stick with what I bought from the seed shop last year — it did alright, about 250 kg of lint per mu. I'll buy fresh seed, not saved seed, because hybrid cotton you can't save. Fertilizer — I put down one bag of compound (复合肥) per mu before planting, then topdress urea when it starts flowering. Middle school math tells me that's around 15 kg of N per mu total, somewhere in there. I'm not going to weigh it exactly.

**On wheat** — standard practice. Plant mid-October after I clear the maize. I use the improved variety everyone in the village uses, 济麦 something, I forget the number. Base fertilizer with the planter, then topdress urea at jointing in early spring if the plants look yellow. Four irrigations usually — one before winter, then jointing, heading, grain filling. The well costs money to run, electricity isn't free, but wheat without water here gets you maybe 200 kg instead of 400.

**On maize** — the window between wheat harvest and maize planting is tight, maybe 4-5 days. I hire the neighbor's boy with his machine to do both in one pass — harvest wheat and plant maize directly. Costs about 60 yuan per mu but it saves a week. Hybrid seed, same brand I used last year because it handled that dry spell in August. Fertilizer once at planting, maybe topdress if I see the leaves going pale.

**Money-wise** — cash is tight. Fertilizer prices went up again this spring. I'll spend what I have to spend but I'm not going to buy extra urea "just in case." If the weather is bad I can always buy more later. The problem is at my age I can't carry the bags like I used to, so I try to get the seed shop to deliver.

**What I'm worried about:** My knee has been bad since winter. If I can't do the cotton picking in September-October, I'll have to hire women from the village — that's 100-120 yuan a day, and we'd need 15-20 person-days. That would eat half the cotton profit. But I'm not going to quit cotton yet. Maybe next year.
